predecessors.name: Scythian kingdom
predecessors.text: a limited territory which included the steppes and foothills of Crimea until Taurida, the lower Dnieper, and the lower Southern Bug rivers

successors.name: Kingdom of Pontus
successors.text: central and western Crimea except Chersonesus, plus a significant part of the northwest Pontic region, including Pontic Olbia

ledger.x: c. 200 BCE: the Scythian kingdom of Crimea stands on the steppes and foothills of Crimea. The page says it was 'created by the Scythians during the 3rd century BCE' and refounded in the mid-2nd century BCE; the map start year is a bridge.
Mid-2nd century BCE: Skilurus extends the kingdom over central and western Crimea and the northwest Pontic region including Olbia.
c. 110-108 BCE: Diophantus captures the Scythian fortresses including Neapolis and annexes the land to Pontus.
c. 109 BCE: King Palacus is defeated and the kingdom ends.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontiers or dates for the first kingdom's extent.
